events.title: Galileo Observes Neptune
events.description: Galileo Galilei observed the planet Neptune through his telescope and recorded it in his notes, but he mistook it for a fixed star. Neptune would not be formally identified as a planet until 1846.
events.significance: This was the first recorded sighting of Neptune, showing how early telescopic astronomy captured the outer solar system more than two centuries before the planet's official discovery.

events.title: John C. Calhoun Resigns the Vice Presidency
events.description: John C. Calhoun resigned as Vice President of the United States under Andrew Jackson, following bitter disputes over the Nullification Crisis and tariff policy. He was the first U.S. Vice President to resign from office.
events.significance: The resignation highlighted the deep tension between states' rights and federal authority, a conflict that would later contribute to the sectional divisions leading to the American Civil War.

events.title: First Commercial Public Film Screening by the Lumière Brothers
events.description: The Lumière brothers, Auguste and Louis, held the first public commercial screening of projected motion pictures to a paying audience at the Salon Indien du Grand Café in Paris.
events.significance: This event is widely regarded as the birth of cinema as a commercial medium, launching what would become one of the most influential art forms and industries of the 20th century.

events.title: Messina Earthquake and Tsunami
events.description: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck the Strait of Messina in southern Italy, followed by a devastating tsunami. The cities of Messina and Reggio Calabria were almost entirely destroyed, with an estimated 75,000 to 200,000 deaths.
events.significance: It remains one of the deadliest earthquakes in European history and led to major advances in seismic-resistant building regulations in Italy.

events.title: Birth of Woodrow Wilson
events.description: Thomas Woodrow Wilson, the future 28th President of the United States, was born in Staunton, Virginia. He later served as president from 1913 to 1921, led the country through World War I, and championed the League of Nations.
events.significance: Wilson's presidency reshaped American domestic policy through Progressive reforms and redefined the U.S. role in international affairs, and he received the 1919 Nobel Peace Prize.
